items.name: HyperFrames

Commands: init, preview, check, render (mp4, webm, mov with alpha, gif, png-sequence, hls), plus lint, snapshot, doctor, cloud render and Lambda render. Init can transcribe an audio file with whisper. Project ships AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md so an agent knows how to author. 5,399 commits, 5.3k forks.

items.why: RAN HERE: scaffold plus a 10-second 1920x1080 30 fps H.264 render took 23 s in draft quality on this CPU-only sandbox (about 2.3 s of render per second of video); sandbox could not download its preferred chrome-headless-shell, so it fell back to screenshot capture, which it says is slower; I pointed it at an installed Chromium with HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH It refuses to render when its own check finds a correctness warning: the starter loads GSAP from a CDN, which this sandbox blocks, and the render failed until I vendored GSAP locally. Good safety behaviour, but vendor GSAP and fonts for any offline or locked-down machine Anonymous usage telemetry exists (project and render events, per-skill attribution). I set DO_NOT_TRACK and HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY but did NOT verify those names are honoured: check its docs before running on a work machine Needs Node 22+, ffmpeg; each render worker is a separate Chrome (about 256 MB RAM each); an 8 GB machine is fine for 1080p, long 4K renders untested HeyGen-hosted cloud rendering and a desktop Studio are offered; pricing not shown; the repo says no per-render fees or commercial thresholds for the framework itself Young release line (0.8.x): pin the version

items.name: OpenCreator (formerly KrillinAI)
items.description: Desktop creator workspace (macOS, Windows) driven by Codex CLI: video download and translation, image/video/voice generation, writing tools and agent chat; providers include OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, Gemini, Kling, Seedance, MiniMax and Edge TTS; local transcription via faster-whisper/whisper.cpp; data kept locally in SQLite. Optional paid account with credits via Stripe. Last commit 2026-10-16.
items.verdictNote: conditional: only for video translation/dubbing
items.why: Its KrillinAI roots (subtitle translation and dubbing) are the useful part; as a full workspace it is Codex/OpenAI-centred and duplicates a Claude-based pipeline. Many look-alike forks exist: use krillinai/OpenCreator only. Edge TTS is an unofficial Microsoft route with commercial-use doubts.

items.name: Short Video Factory
items.description: Cross-platform desktop app (v1.3.0, 2026-10-16) that turns a prompt plus your footage clips into batches of product-marketing short videos: AI copy via any OpenAI-compatible API, voiceover, auto editing, subtitles, effects. Chinese and English UI.
items.verdictNote: skip for now
items.why: Voice is Edge TTS only (unofficial Microsoft route; commercial use questionable), built for e-commerce product clips, and duplicates an HTML/ffmpeg or HyperFrames pipeline. AGPL is fine for desktop use.

items.name: Podcastfy
items.description: Turns URLs, PDFs, text or images into two-host podcast conversations in many languages; transcripts from 100+ LLMs (local supported); TTS via OpenAI, Google, ElevenLabs or Edge. Python 3.11+, ffmpeg. Last commit 2026-05-04 (README only).
items.verdictNote: assess: idea good, project slowing
items.why: No local TTS out of the box, so every episode costs TTS fees unless you patch in a local voice; recent commits are README updates only. Worth a test only if an audio-podcast channel is planned.

items.name: Social Media Agent (LangChain)
items.description: LangGraph agent: URL in, X and LinkedIn post drafts out, reviewed in an Agent Inbox (approve/edit/reject) and scheduled. Needs Anthropic API, FireCrawl, Arcade, LangSmith; full setup adds Vertex AI, X/LinkedIn developer apps, GitHub token, Supabase, Slack. Maintained (fix 2026-10-12).
items.verdictNote: reference: copy the review pattern
items.why: Six-plus services and keys for something an n8n flow plus a scheduler like Postiz already does; the human-in-the-loop Agent Inbox is the idea worth copying. X API posting has its own costs.

items.name: Poly Haven
items.description: Free HDRIs, PBR textures and 3D models, all CC0: commercial use, no attribution, redistribution allowed. blender-mcp can pull Poly Haven assets directly into Blender.
items.why: Best zero-risk source for lighting, surfaces and props. CC0 covers the assets only (logos, renders and site text are not CC0), and the Terms of Service forbid scraping or data mining without permission, so download normally rather than bulk-harvesting.

items.name: ambientCG
items.description: 2,000+ PBR materials, HDRIs, decals, atlases, terrains and some models under CC0 1.0 Universal; commercial use without permission or credit.
items.why: Complements Poly Haven for realistic surfaces; CC0 with no attribution needed. Supporter tiers exist on Patreon/Ko-fi but assets stay free.

items.name: Quaternius
items.description: Low-poly characters, props, environment mega-kits and retargetable humanoid animation libraries (Universal Animation Library 1 and 2), well suited to lightweight web games.
items.why: Licence is the Quaternius Asset License v1.0, NOT CC0 as often claimed: royalty-free in commercial games, no credit needed, but you may not sell or redistribute the assets themselves (even modified), so never commit raw packs to a public repo. Some packs sit behind Patreon; check each pack's licence.

items.name: Mixamo
items.description: Adobe's free auto-rigger and animation library: upload a humanoid character, get a rig and apply animations in one click; FBX export.
items.why: Free with an Adobe ID and royalty-free for personal, commercial and non-profit projects including video games (Adobe FAQ). Not available to Enterprise/Federated IDs or China accounts. The FAQ (last updated 2021) does not cover redistributing raw files or AI training: use it to animate characters, never as model-training data. Humanoids only.

items.name: Babylon.js
items.description: Full browser 3D game engine in TypeScript (scenes, physics, GUI, WebXR) with an online Playground, glTF Sandbox and shader tools. v9.17.0 tagged 2026-07-16.
items.why: More complete game engine than three.js (which is mainly a renderer). Worth it only if a 3D browser game outgrows a custom engine or three.js; pick one 3D stack per game rather than mixing.

items.name: Godot Engine
items.description: Free, open-source 2D/3D game engine under MIT; no royalties or fees; one-click export including web. Agent bridges: godot-ai and godot-mcp (see mcp-servers).
items.why: Already part of the toolset for side projects and prototypes; MIT means no revenue share. Check web-export size and browser support per project (not verified here).

items.name: comic-maker (Aillex)
items.description: One sentence to a lettered comic, fully local: Ollama writes the script (characters with locked looks, pages, panels, dialogue, SFX), ComfyUI renders each panel (Z-Image Turbo by default; swappable in ~30 lines), a PIL compositor adds layouts of 1-9 panels, speech bubbles, SFX, title strip and CBZ export. Styles: sunday-strip, manga, noir, euro-album. Last commit 2026-07-20.
items.verdictNote: trial first: best fit for a local Ollama + ComfyUI stack
items.why: No cloud, no credits, MIT, stages runnable separately with a hand-editable script.json. Early cut (7 files) and consistency relies on seeds plus restated looks, not a trained character model. VRAM of the default Z-Image Turbo checkpoint not checked; swap in an 8 GB-friendly model if needed.

items.verdictNote: reference: copy targeted panel edits

items.description: Single image to 3D mesh in under 0.5 s on an A100; about 6 GB VRAM by default; vertex colours by default, optional baked texture. Last commit 2026-06-04.

items.why: Fits 8 GB. Stable Fast 3D is its successor with better UVs and textures, but SF3D needs Stability registration and visible 'Powered by Stability AI' credit; TripoSR is plain MIT with no such strings. Quality is prototype-grade: use for greybox props, then refine.

items.name: Drei
items.description: Ready-made helpers for React Three Fiber: camera controls, environments, skies, shadows, text, model loading and more. Last commit 2026-09-30.
items.verdictNote: adopt if the game or site is built on React Three Fiber
items.why: The standard companion to React Three Fiber; saves days of boilerplate. Only relevant if the stack is React; a plain three.js or custom engine gets nothing from it.

items.name: React Postprocessing
items.description: Post-processing effects for React Three Fiber (bloom, depth of field, noise, vignette and more), wrapping the postprocessing library. Last commit 2026-10-19.
items.verdictNote: conditional on a React Three Fiber stack
items.why: Biggest visual upgrade per line of code for R3F scenes; each effect costs GPU time, so test on phones before shipping.

items.name: NVIDIA SimReady Central (Hugging Face)
items.description: Open library of simulation-ready OpenUSD 3D assets on Hugging Face (2,000+ at launch; the browser showed about 3,600 in industrial, OEM, residential, hospital and lighting categories). Each asset carries physics data (collision shapes, mass, friction) for robot simulation in Isaac Sim and other OpenUSD tools, with natural-language search and filters for licence, mass and size. Contributors such as NVIDIA (Warehouse-01, 753 assets, CC-BY-4.0, about 10-15 GB), Yaskawa (robot arms, Apache-2.0) and Robotiq (gripper, CC-BY-4.0) host their own datasets; most need a free Hugging Face login and accepting access terms.
items.verdictNote: adopt: free source for robot-simulation scenes; check each asset's own licence
items.why: Physics data is already set up, which saves the slowest part of building a simulation scene. The hub's Apache-2.0 tag covers only the catalog: each contributor sets the asset licence, so filter by licence. CC-BY-4.0 and Apache-2.0 allow commercial use with credit; brand names and product likenesses (Yaskawa, Robotiq) are still trademarks. Opens in Blender as plain geometry if you don't need physics.

items.name: cgbookcase
items.description: Free high-quality PBR textures (wood, stone, metal and more) up to 8K, plus decals.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0 1.0
items.why: Commercial use yes, no attribution needed. Smaller catalogue than Poly Haven.

items.name: ShareTextures
items.description: Free PBR textures, some 3D models and atlases, many up to 4K/8K.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0 1.0
items.why: Commercial use yes, no attribution needed. Funded by Patreon; a few extras may be gated to supporters.

items.name: 3DTextures.me
items.description: Hundreds of free seamless PBR textures with Blender-ready maps. Patreon gives higher resolutions.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0 1.0
items.why: Commercial use yes, no attribution. Free downloads are mostly 2K, with higher resolutions on Patreon.

items.name: TextureCan
items.description: Free seamless PBR textures in common categories, with packed maps for game engines.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0 1.0
items.why: Commercial use yes, no attribution. Quality varies, so check maps before use.

items.name: Textures.com (free tier)
items.description: Huge library of photo textures, PBR materials, decals and HDRIs. A free account gets a small daily credit allowance at limited resolution.
items.verdictNote: trial: Textures.com proprietary royalty-free licence
items.why: Commercial use in your projects is allowed, but you can't redistribute the raw textures (for example, inside open-source repos or asset packs). Free credits are small (historically about 15/day) and limited to low resolution.

items.name: Poliigon free assets
items.description: A rotating set of free studio-quality textures, HDRIs and models from a mostly paid library. Includes a Blender add-on.
items.verdictNote: trial: Poliigon licence (royalty-free, no redistribution)
items.why: Commercial use yes, no attribution. You can't redistribute the raw files and need an account. Only a small part of the library is free.

items.name: HDRMaps (freebies)
items.description: Commercial HDRI store with a sizeable free section of skies and interiors.
items.verdictNote: trial: HDRMaps royalty-free licence
items.why: Commercial renders and games are allowed, but you can't redistribute or resell the HDRIs. Some free items are lower resolution than the paid versions.

items.name: HDRI-Skies
items.description: Sky-focused HDRI store with a free collection (sunsets, overcast, clear skies).
items.verdictNote: trial: HDRI-Skies royalty-free licence
items.why: Commercial use is allowed for renders and products; redistributing the HDRIs is not. Only part of the library is free.

items.name: iHDRI
items.description: A small set of free high-res HDRI panoramas by Peter Sanitra. Updated rarely.
items.verdictNote: assess: Custom free licence (no redistribution)
items.why: Believed free for commercial renders with no redistribution, but read the licence before shipping. Small and possibly stale catalogue.

items.name: LEOMOON Free IES Lights Pack
items.description: A pack of about 100 IES light profiles for realistic spotlight and downlight falloff in Blender, Unreal and other renderers.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Free for personal and commercial use
items.why: Commercial use yes, but don't resell or redistribute the pack itself. IES suits Blender/Cycles and offline renders more than Godot or three.js.
items.license: Free for personal and commercial use

items.name: IES Library (ieslibrary.com)
items.description: A searchable collection of real manufacturer IES photometric files for accurate architectural lighting.
items.verdictNote: trial: Manufacturer photometric data, free to download
items.why: Fine for lighting renders commercially, but terms belong to each manufacturer, so don't repackage or redistribute the files.
items.license: Manufacturer photometric data, free to download

items.name: Shadertoy
items.description: The largest gallery of GLSL fragment shaders. Great for learning and inspiration, and easy to port to three.js or Godot.
items.verdictNote: reference: Default CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 unless author states otherwise
items.why: Default licence is non-commercial, so don't ship this code in monetised games or videos unless the author's header grants a permissive licence (some use MIT/CC0).
items.license: Default CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 unless author states otherwise

items.name: BlenderKit (now Blendkit)
items.description: Add-on based library for Blender, with Godot (4.0+), Maya and Rhino add-ons as of 2026. About 67k free assets (around 22k models, 36k materials, 4k HDRIs, 1k brushes) out of 140k+ total, with the rest paid ($17.90/mo or $118.80/yr under $100k revenue, $48/mo for businesses).
items.verdictNote: adopt: Royalty Free or CC0 (per asset)
items.why: Both free licences allow commercial use: CC0 assets need no credit, while Royalty Free assets can be used in your work but not redistributed as raw files. The domain now redirects to blendkit.com, and the official licence page didn't load, so terms are confirmed only through CG Channel (Aug 2026).

items.name: Material Maker
items.description: Open-source node-based procedural material and texture authoring tool, built on Godot and similar to Substance Designer. Exports to Godot, Unity, Unreal and PNG maps.
items.verdictNote: adopt: MIT (tool); your outputs are yours
items.why: Free and commercial-safe, with no attribution needed for the materials you make. Smaller node library and community than Substance.

items.name: ArmorPaint
items.description: Standalone 3D PBR texture painter, similar to Substance Painter. Includes node materials and a Blender bridge.
items.verdictNote: trial: Source zlib (ArmorTools); prebuilt binaries paid
items.why: Commercial use of your outputs is fine. Official binaries cost a small one-time fee (about €20), or you can build them free from the open-source repo. Less polished than Substance.

items.name: Adobe Substance 3D Assets (free and community)
items.description: Large .sbsar and PBR material library. A subset of free and community materials is available with an Adobe account, the rest needs a Substance subscription.
items.verdictNote: assess: Adobe Substance 3D Assets licence; community assets per their own terms
items.why: Generally commercial use in renders and games, no raw redistribution. Read the licence for free vs. subscription assets. .sbsar files need Substance tools or the Blender plugin.
items.license: Adobe Substance 3D Assets licence; community assets per their own terms

items.name: Lospec Palette List
items.description: Thousands of curated pixel-art palettes, exportable as PNG, GPL, ASE or hex for Aseprite, Godot and others.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Colour palettes (not copyrightable; credit appreciated)
items.why: Using a palette commercially is safe since colour lists aren't protected. Crediting the palette author is courtesy, not required. Other Lospec tools and tutorials are just reference.

items.name: Free PBR (freepbr.com)
items.description: A few hundred free PBR materials, mostly 2K, with paid premium and higher-res packs.
items.verdictNote: trial: Free PBR custom licence (commercial OK, no redistribution)
items.why: Commercial use in games and renders is allowed with no attribution, but you can't resell or redistribute the textures. Quality is mixed and some maps are older.
items.license: Free PBR custom licence (commercial OK, no redistribution)

items.name: Pixar One Twenty Eight
items.description: Pixar's classic set of 128 tileable textures, rereleased with full maps.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC BY 4.0
items.why: Commercial use yes, but you must credit Pixar.

items.name: AMD GPUOpen MaterialX Library
items.description: Hundreds of free PBR materials in MaterialX and texture form, with Blender/USD-friendly downloads.
items.verdictNote: trial: Free royalty-free (per material; many CC0/permissive)
items.why: Commercial use allowed for most materials. Check each material's licence tag. Converting MaterialX to Godot or three.js may need baking.

items.name: Physically Based (physicallybased.info)
items.description: Database of measured PBR values (base colour, IOR, roughness, light temperatures) for real materials and light sources.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0 1.0 (data)
items.why: Free data with no attribution needed. A reference for tuning materials and lights, not a texture source.

items.name: CMU Graphics Lab Motion Capture Database
items.description: About 2,600 classic mocap clips (walks, sports, dance and more) in ASF/AMC, with community BVH and FBX conversions.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CMU notice: free to use, modify and share; may be included in commercial products but not resold as raw data; acknowledgement requested for publications
items.why: Commercial use inside a game or video is allowed. You cannot resell the raw data itself, and credit is only asked for in publications. The catches: it is 2000s-era data that needs cleanup and retargeting, and the official site would not open from here, so the terms come from a mirror that quotes CMU's notice.
items.license: CMU notice: free to use, modify and share; may be included in commercial products but not resold as raw data; acknowledgement requested for publications

items.name: Rokoko Studio Starter + Rokoko Video + Motion Library
items.description: Free Studio for mocap cleanup and FBX export. It includes 30 seconds a month of AI video-to-mocap (Vision AI) and unlimited text-to-motion clips, though only 5 a month can be added to Studio. It also has a mocap marketplace with free clips.
items.verdictNote: trial: Starter plan free forever; Motion Library animations usable in any project including commercial
items.why: Motion Library clips are cleared for commercial use. The pricing page does not separately confirm commercial rights for free-tier video captures. The free tier is small (30 s a month, FBX only, cloud upload). BVH export starts at $28 a month (Plus), and Basic is $12 a month.
items.license: Starter plan free forever; Motion Library animations usable in any project including commercial

items.name: Reallusion AccuRIG
items.description: Free desktop auto-rigger for Windows. It rigs a static humanoid mesh (body and fingers) and exports FBX or USD for Blender, Unity, Unreal and Godot.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Free software; Reallusion staff: usable for personal and commercial projects; the rigged character keeps its own licence
items.why: Commercial use is OK and the output is not tied to any engine. The only licence that matters is your mesh's own licence. The commercial-use confirmation comes from a staff reply on the Reallusion forum, not a EULA page.
items.license: Free software; Reallusion staff: usable for personal and commercial projects; the rigged character keeps its own licence

items.name: Reallusion ActorCore free motions
items.description: About 32 free mocap motions alongside 4,000+ paid clips, downloadable as FBX after retargeting to an AccuRIG or ActorCore rig.
items.verdictNote: assess: ActorCore content EULA (exact export terms for free motions not confirmed)
items.why: The free set is small: Reallusion staff say only 32 clips are free, not 4,000+. I could not open the licence for games or videos, so read ActorCore's EULA before shipping these in a game.
items.license: ActorCore content EULA (exact export terms for free motions not confirmed)

items.name: Bandai Namco Research Motiondataset
items.description: High-quality stylised motion datasets (walks and actions in many styles) in BVH, released by Bandai Namco Research.
items.verdictNote: skip: CC BY-NC 4.0 (data); MIT (Blender scripts)
items.why: Non-commercial only, so it cannot go into monetised YouTube videos or a paid game. Use it only for study or personal tests.

items.name: Truebones free mocap
items.description: Large free BVH/FBX mocap packs (humans and many animals) given away on Gumroad, alongside paid packs.
items.verdictNote: trial: Truebones terms: products 'absolutely royalty free', usable for any purpose including commercial (full text truncated)
items.why: The terms say royalty-free with commercial use allowed, but the page was cut off, so read the full terms PDF before shipping. Some free packs are adult-themed, so choose carefully. Quality varies.
items.license: Truebones terms: products 'absolutely royalty free', usable for any purpose including commercial (full text truncated)

items.name: Blender Rigify
items.description: Blender's built-in modular rig generator. It builds full animator-friendly human, quadruped and other rigs from meta-rigs.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Bundled with Blender (GPL software; your rigs and animations are yours)
items.why: Commercial use is fine and there are no limits. The catch is that the generated control rig is complex. For game export you usually bake the motion to the deform bones, or use a game-rig converter.
items.license: Bundled with Blender (GPL software; your rigs and animations are yours)

items.name: MPFB2 (MakeHuman for Blender)
items.description: Free open-source Blender add-on for generating realistic rigged human characters, with Rigify and game-rig options.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Core assets (base mesh, targets, skins) CC0; exported characters usable commercially; third-party assets keep their own licences
items.why: Commercial use is OK with no attribution for the CC0 core assets. Check the licence of any community clothes or hair you add.
items.license: Core assets (base mesh, targets, skins) CC0; exported characters usable commercially; third-party assets keep their own licences

items.name: VRoid Studio
items.description: Free anime-style character creator for Windows, Mac and iPad. It exports rigged VRM avatars that import into Blender, Godot (godot-vrm) and three.js (three-vrm).
items.verdictNote: trial: Free app; creator sets per-model VRM conditions (commercial/corporate use, attribution); pixiv's own terms for output not re-verified
items.why: Your own creations are generally usable commercially, and you set the permission flags in the VRM yourself. I only confirmed the VRM conditions-of-use spec, not pixiv's Studio terms page. The anime look only.
items.license: Free app; creator sets per-model VRM conditions (commercial/corporate use, attribution); pixiv's own terms for output not re-verified

items.name: Ready Player Me
items.description: Former cross-platform avatar creator and SDK.
items.verdictNote: skip: Service discontinued
items.why: Dead. Netflix acquired it in Dec 2025, and the public services, API and SDKs shut down on 31 Jan 2026. Do not build on it.

items.name: DeepMotion Animate 3D
items.description: Cloud AI that turns video into mocap with face and hand tracking. The free tier gives 60 seconds of animation a month.
items.verdictNote: assess: Freemium accounts: personal, non-commercial use only; commercial requires paid plan
items.why: Free-tier output cannot be used commercially, so monetised YouTube or games need a paid plan. Videos are uploaded to the cloud.
items.license: Freemium accounts: personal, non-commercial use only; commercial requires paid plan

items.name: Move.ai (Move One)
items.description: Single-camera AI mocap from a phone video (the Move One app) plus a multicam option. Gen 1 uses 1 credit per person-second and Gen 2 uses 2.
items.verdictNote: trial: Free account: one-time 30 credits; paid from $18/mo (60 credits); commercial terms not confirmed
items.why: The free trial is tiny: 30 one-time credits, so roughly 15 to 30 seconds, with clips capped at 30 s. Processing happens in the cloud. Commercial-use terms were not on the pricing page, so check the ToS before using it for monetised content.
items.license: Free account: one-time 30 credits; paid from $18/mo (60 credits); commercial terms not confirmed

items.name: FreeMoCap
items.description: Open-source markerless mocap that runs locally from one or more ordinary webcams. It exports to Blender, with optional NVIDIA GPU acceleration.
items.verdictNote: trial: AGPL-3.0 (software); your captured motion data is yours
items.why: Free and local with no cloud and no credits, and the AGPL covers only the software, not your animations. The setup is technical, and good results need 2 or more calibrated cameras.
items.license: AGPL-3.0 (software); your captured motion data is yours

items.name: Cascadeur
items.description: Physics-assisted keyframe animation tool with AI auto-posing, plus video mocap features.
items.verdictNote: assess: Free: non-commercial only, .casc export only; Indie $12 list ($8 discounted), for revenue under $100k/yr, FBX/DAE/USD export; Pro $49
items.why: The free plan cannot be used commercially and cannot export FBX, so it is really a learning tool. Indie at about $8 to $12 is the cheap commercial path for revenue under $100k a year.
items.license: Free: non-commercial only, .casc export only; Indie $12 list ($8 discounted), for revenue under $100k/yr, FBX/DAE/USD export; Pro $49

items.name: Plask Motion
items.description: Browser-based AI video-to-mocap and animation editor. It was still operating as of 2026.
items.verdictNote: trial: Free plan: 15 s/day mocap, 1 GB, FBX/GLB/BVH export; Standard $18/mo, Pro $50/mo (annual); commercial terms not confirmed
items.why: The daily free quota is useful, but processing is in the cloud. I could not confirm whether free-plan output may be used commercially, so read the ToS before monetising.
items.license: Free plan: 15 s/day mocap, 1 GB, FBX/GLB/BVH export; Standard $18/mo, Pro $50/mo (annual); commercial terms not confirmed

items.name: Universal Animation Library (Quaternius)
items.description: 120+ game animations on one humanoid rig in FBX/GLB for Godot, Unity and Unreal. The free Standard tier has 45 clips, Pro is $9.99 and Source is $14.99.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0 1.0
items.why: Commercial use with no attribution. This is the Quaternius pack, so drop it if Quaternius is already listed.

items.name: Unreal Game Animation Sample Project (GASP)
items.description: 500+ AAA-quality locomotion and motion-matching animations from Epic.
items.verdictNote: skip: Free; Epic content licensed for use with Unreal Engine only
items.why: Commercial use is allowed, but only inside Unreal Engine. You cannot export it to Godot, Blender game pipelines or three.js.
items.license: Free; Epic content licensed for use with Unreal Engine only

items.name: Mesh2Motion
items.description: Free open-source browser alternative to Mixamo. You import a GLB/GLTF/FBX mesh, fit a human, quadruped or bird skeleton, and export animated GLB.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Code MIT; bundled rigs and animations CC0
items.why: Commercial use is fine with no attribution, and it outputs GLB that works in Godot and three.js. The library is smaller than Mixamo's, and the auto-weighting can need fixes in Blender.
items.license: Code MIT; bundled rigs and animations CC0

items.name: Auto-Rig Pro (Blender add-on)
items.description: Popular Blender auto-rigger. Full adds Smart auto-placement, Remap retargeting (for mocap and BVH onto your rig) and clean FBX/glTF game export.
items.verdictNote: trial: GPL add-on; Lite $25, Full $50 (includes 12 months of updates)
items.why: A one-time $50 removes most retargeting and export pain, and your output is yours to use commercially. It is optional, since Rigify plus free tools cover the basics.
items.license: GPL add-on; Lite $25, Full $50 (includes 12 months of updates)

items.name: Kenney Animated Characters
items.description: Small rigged low-poly characters with swappable skins and basic idle, run and jump animations.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0 1.0
items.why: Commercial use with no attribution, and good for prototypes and stylised games. They have very few animations, so combine them with other libraries via retargeting.

items.name: Godot 4 skeleton retargeting (built-in)
items.description: Godot's importer can map any humanoid skeleton to a standard humanoid profile (BoneMap/SkeletonProfileHumanoid), so one set of animations can be shared across characters.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Part of Godot Engine (MIT)
items.why: Free, with commercial use OK. It lets you mix clips from CMU, Mesh2Motion and other sources on your own rigs inside Godot. The catch: the bone mapping sometimes needs manual fixes. I could open the page but its text was not returned, so this rests on Godot's MIT licence as known.

items.name: Kenney
items.description: Hundreds of game asset packs (2D, 3D, UI, audio) from Kenney. The 3D kits (city, racing, furniture, nature, castle, space and more) come as FBX/OBJ/GLB, and an All-in-1 bundle is sold on itch.io.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0 1.0
items.why: Commercial use is fine and no credit is needed, because everything on the asset pages is public domain. The one catch is that you can't use the Kenney logo.

items.name: KayKit (Kay Lousberg)
items.description: About 25 cohesive low-poly packs (adventurers, dungeon, medieval builder, platformer, furniture and more) in FBX and glTF that work in Godot, Unity and Unreal. Each pack has a free tier and paid 'Extra' and 'Source' (.blend) tiers.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0 1.0 (free and paid tiers)
items.why: CC0, so commercial use is fine and no credit is needed. The free tier holds only part of each pack, and the author asks that you don't resell the unmodified files.

items.name: Poly Pizza
items.description: Search engine for about 10,600 free low-poly models, including the archived Google Poly collection and Quaternius/Kenney items. Downloads are GLB/FBX/OBJ and need no account.
items.verdictNote: trial: Mostly CC-BY 3.0/4.0, some CC0 (per model)
items.why: Commercial use is OK, but most models are CC-BY, so you must credit the creator; check each model's licence tag. I couldn't open poly.pizza itself; licence details come from secondary 2026 guides.

items.name: Khronos glTF-Sample-Assets
items.description: The official glTF test and showcase models (DamagedHelmet, Sponza, FlightHelmet, material and extension test assets, and more). They are ideal for testing three.js, Godot or Blender glTF pipelines.
items.verdictNote: trial: Per model: mostly CC-BY 4.0, some CC0 or other (see each model's README)
items.why: Most models allow commercial use with credit, but licences differ per model and some have been removed or may be removed. Read each model's README and treat these as test or demo assets, not game content.
items.license: Per model: mostly CC-BY 4.0, some CC0 or other (see each model's README)

items.name: Fab (Epic Games)
items.description: Epic's unified marketplace that replaced the Unreal Marketplace, Sketchfab Store, Quixel and ArtStation Marketplace. It has a year-round community free section, rotating limited-time free packs every two weeks, and a free Megascans starter set. Also a source of free animation packs and materials; Epic's own UE-only content (e.g. Game Animation Sample) can't leave Unreal.
items.verdictNote: trial: Fab Standard (Personal <$100k revenue / Professional >$100k), CC-BY, legacy UE Marketplace licence
items.why: Standard licence assets can be used commercially; CC-BY items need credit. Watch for the legacy UE-only licence on some migrated items. Assets tagged NoAI can't be used for AI training. The licence doc doesn't say outright that Standard covers non-Unreal engines, so check the EULA or each listing before using one in Godot or three.js.
items.license: Fab Standard (Personal <$100k revenue / Professional >$100k), CC-BY, legacy UE Marketplace licence

items.name: Quixel Megascans (via Fab)
items.description: Photogrammetry scan library, now sold on Fab. Free access to the full library ended 31 Dec 2024; a free starter set (about 1,500 assets) and occasional free promotions remain. Bridge is being deprecated, and new assets stopped appearing there in early 2026.
items.verdictNote: assess: Fab Standard (new); legacy Megascans terms for assets downloaded before 2025
items.why: Most of the library is paid now, and the Standard licence allows commercial use. Anything you already claimed or downloaded keeps its old terms, so back it up. The status comes from secondary 2026 sources, not an official Epic page.
items.license: Fab Standard (new); legacy Megascans terms for assets downloaded before 2025

items.name: Sketchfab (downloadable CC models)
items.description: Hundreds of thousands of downloadable models, with search filters by licence, including CC0-only. Downloads come as the original file, glTF/GLB or USDZ. The store moved to Fab in Oct 2024, and ownership reportedly moved from Epic to KitBash in Aug 2026.
items.verdictNote: trial: Per model: CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC, CC BY-ND (plus Standard/Editorial on legacy store items)
items.why: Filter to CC0 or CC BY for commercial use (CC BY needs credit); avoid NC and ND for monetized videos and games. Free downloads still worked as of Sep 2026, but Epic had earlier planned to remove free licensing and the future under KitBash is unclear, so download what you need now.
items.license: Per model: CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC, CC BY-ND (plus Standard/Editorial on legacy store items)

items.name: OpenGameArt.org
items.description: Long-running community archive of free game art, including 3D models, textures and audio; it also mirrors many Kenney and KayKit packs. Quality varies a lot. Also has textures, particle/effect sheets and game audio.
items.verdictNote: trial: CC0, CC-BY 3.0/4.0, CC-BY-SA 3.0/4.0, OGA-BY 3.0/4.0, GPL 2.0/3.0 (per asset)
items.why: Commercial use is allowed under all five licences, but all except CC0 require credit. CC-BY-SA and GPL are copyleft, so avoid them for closed-source games, and CC-BY and CC-BY-SA forbid DRM distribution. Preview images are all rights reserved.
items.license: CC0, CC-BY 3.0/4.0, CC-BY-SA 3.0/4.0, OGA-BY 3.0/4.0, GPL 2.0/3.0 (per asset)

items.name: itch.io free game assets
items.description: Huge indie asset storefront (about 53k free asset packs across 2D and 3D as of Sep 2026) with pay-what-you-want packs. Home of KayKit, Quaternius mirrors and many low-poly creators.
items.verdictNote: trial: Mixed, set by each creator (CC0, CC-BY, custom 'free for commercial use' terms, etc.)
items.why: Many packs allow commercial use, but each creator writes their own terms, sometimes only in the description. Read every pack page, and don't rely on the site's licence filter, which covers only a few licence types.
items.license: Mixed, set by each creator (CC0, CC-BY, custom 'free for commercial use' terms, etc.)

items.name: Blender demo files and Blender Studio assets
items.description: Official demo scenes and asset bundles (such as the CC0 Human Base Meshes bundle, pose libraries and splash scenes) plus Blender Studio open-movie characters, rigs and assets. Some Studio downloads may need a subscription.
items.verdictNote: trial: Demo files: CC0, CC-BY or CC-BY-SA per file; Blender Studio: generally CC-BY (Blender Foundation)
items.why: Commercial use is OK under CC0 and CC-BY (CC-BY needs credit to the Blender Foundation or the artist). CC-BY-SA files are share-alike, so avoid them for closed products, and check each file's listed licence.
items.license: Demo files: CC0, CC-BY or CC-BY-SA per file; Blender Studio: generally CC-BY (Blender Foundation)

items.name: NASA 3D Resources
items.description: Growing collection of spacecraft, rover, asteroid and planetary models, plus textures and 3D-print files, mirrored on GitHub (nasa/NASA-3D-Resources).
items.verdictNote: adopt: Public domain / 'free and without copyright' (US Gov work) subject to NASA media usage guidelines
items.why: Free to use, including commercially. The catch is that you must not use the NASA insignia or 'meatball' logo or imply NASA endorsement (per NASA brand guidelines). Model quality and format vary.
items.license: Public domain / 'free and without copyright' (US Gov work) subject to NASA media usage guidelines

items.name: Objaverse / Objaverse-XL
items.description: Research datasets: Objaverse 1.0 has about 800k annotated objects (from Sketchfab), and XL has about 10.8M objects scraped from Sketchfab, GitHub, Thingiverse, Smithsonian and Polycam.
items.verdictNote: reference: Dataset: ODC-By 1.0; each object keeps its own licence (CC variants incl. NC, MIT, GPL, many unlisted)
items.why: Built for ML research, not as an asset library. Licences are mixed or missing per object, and Polycam data is non-commercial by request only, so don't ship these in products unless you check each object's source licence.
items.license: Dataset: ODC-By 1.0; each object keeps its own licence (CC variants incl. NC, MIT, GPL, many unlisted)

items.name: CGTrader (free models)
items.description: Large marketplace with a big free section (150k+ free models reported) of very mixed quality; free downloads need an account.
items.verdictNote: trial: Royalty Free or Editorial (per model)
items.why: Royalty Free models can be used commercially, including in games, but you can't resell or redistribute the raw files. Editorial models are non-commercial only (e.g., branded cars), so check the licence on every free model.

items.name: TurboSquid (free models)
items.description: Shutterstock-owned marketplace with a free section; free downloads need an account and fall under the same licence as purchases.
items.verdictNote: trial: TurboSquid Royalty Free License (Editorial-labelled items restricted)
items.why: Commercial use in games and videos is allowed, but game files must be packed so models can't easily be extracted. Free models carry no indemnity, Editorial items can't be used commercially, and AI or ML use needs prior permission.
items.license: TurboSquid Royalty Free License (Editorial-labelled items restricted)

items.name: Free3D
items.description: User-uploaded model site (TurboSquid network) with lots of free models of uneven quality and little curation.
items.verdictNote: reference: Paid: TurboSquid Royalty Free; free items: uploader-set terms (often 'personal use only')
items.why: Free models often carry personal-use-only or vague uploader terms and no indemnity, so commercial use is risky unless an item clearly says royalty-free. Licence info comes from a third-party summary, not Free3D's own page.
items.license: Paid: TurboSquid Royalty Free; free items: uploader-set terms (often 'personal use only')

items.name: Thingiverse
items.description: Over 1 million 3D-printing designs (mainly STL). Reportedly owned by MyMiniFactory since Feb 2026 (previously UltiMaker/MakerBot).
items.verdictNote: reference: Uploader-chosen: Creative Commons variants (BY, BY-SA, BY-NC, BY-NC-SA, etc.), GPL, public domain
items.why: Mostly print-oriented meshes, not game-ready. Many use NonCommercial licences and most need credit, so commercial use is only OK where the licence is CC0, CC-BY or CC-BY-SA.
items.license: Uploader-chosen: Creative Commons variants (BY, BY-SA, BY-NC, BY-NC-SA, etc.), GPL, public domain

items.name: Printables (Prusa)
items.description: Prusa's 3D-printing model community with a large catalog of STL/3MF designs; licences are irrevocable once published.
items.verdictNote: reference: Uploader-chosen: Creative Commons variants, GNU, BSD, Apache 2.0, CERN OHL, Standard Digital File License, commercial-use licences
items.why: Print-oriented and not game-ready, with many NonCommercial or Standard Digital File (personal-use) licences. Use only items clearly under CC0, CC-BY or a commercial licence, and give credit.
items.license: Uploader-chosen: Creative Commons variants, GNU, BSD, Apache 2.0, CERN OHL, Standard Digital File License, commercial-use licences

items.name: The Models Resource
items.description: Part of The VG Resource network, which collects and distributes models extracted from video games for viewing and reference.
items.verdictNote: skip: None granted: models extracted from commercial video games; copyright stays with the game publishers
items.why: These are copyrighted game assets (Nintendo, Sony and others) with no licence to reuse, so you can't use them in your games or monetized videos. The site itself says it is not for commercial use. Reference viewing only.
items.license: None granted: models extracted from commercial video games; copyright stays with the game publishers

items.name: Pixabay Videos (incl. VFX/overlay clips)
items.description: Large free stock-video library that includes particles, smoke, fire, light leaks, green-screen and overlay clips.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Pixabay Content License
items.why: Commercial use is allowed with no attribution needed. You can't resell clips on their own ("standalone"), can't use visible trademarks or brands commercially, and the terms ban bulk or automated downloading.

items.name: Pixabay Music
items.description: Free royalty-free music library allowed in monetized videos, podcasts and OTT content.
items.verdictNote: trial: Pixabay Content License
items.why: Commercial use is allowed with no attribution needed, as long as the track sits inside a larger work. Some contributors register tracks with YouTube Content ID, so claims can happen: avoid tracks with the shield icon, keep your download records and dispute with the licence link. Pixabay's FAQ only covers games and apps for photos, not music.

items.name: Pixabay Sound Effects
items.description: Free SFX library under the same Pixabay licence as its music and video.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Pixabay Content License
items.why: Commercial use is allowed with no attribution needed. You can't redistribute the files on their own; using them inside a video or game counts as a combined work, which is allowed.

items.name: Mixkit Stock Video
items.description: Envato's free stock-video site; each clip is under either the Free License or the Restricted License.
items.verdictNote: trial: Mixkit Stock Video Free License / Restricted License (per item)
items.why: Free License clips allow commercial use, including monetized YouTube, with no attribution needed. Restricted License clips are for personal, non-commercial use only, so check each clip's label. No resale and no sublicensing.
items.license: Mixkit Stock Video Free License / Restricted License (per item)

items.name: Mixkit Stock Music
items.description: Free curated music for videos, with no attribution needed.
items.verdictNote: trial: Mixkit Stock Music Free License
items.why: Commercial video use, including YouTube, is allowed with no credit needed. A third-party review (not Mixkit's own page) says the licence does not cover video games, broadcast or CDs, and that Mixkit settles Content ID claims if you email them. Confirm the game exclusion on Mixkit's licence page before using any track in a game.

items.name: Mixkit Sound Effects
items.description: Free SFX library with large game, UI and video-game categories.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Mixkit Sound Effects Free License
items.why: Commercial use is allowed with no attribution needed. A secondary guide says the SFX licence explicitly covers video games. You can't resell the files in their original form.

items.name: Pexels Videos
items.description: Large free stock-video library that includes some abstract, particle and overlay footage.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Pexels License
items.why: Commercial use is allowed with no attribution needed. You can't sell unedited copies, redistribute the clips on other stock sites, imply endorsement by people or brands shown, or use clips as a trademark.

items.name: Coverr
items.description: Free stock video and music, with an optional Coverr+ subscription.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Coverr License
items.why: Commercial use is allowed with no credit needed. You can't resell clips, put them into competing stock or template services, or use them for AI training. There are no model or property releases, so recognisable people and brands are your responsibility.

items.name: Videvo
items.description: Stock footage and motion graphics site that mixes free clips (under several licences) with Premium clips (around $14.99/mo).
items.verdictNote: trial: Videvo Attribution License / CC BY 3.0 (free); Premium license (paid)
items.why: Free clips can be used commercially but need credit: to Videvo for Videvo Attribution clips, or to the author for CC BY 3.0 clips. Premium clips need no credit. The licence differs per clip, so check each one. Raw clips can't be redistributed. Videvo's own terms page was blocked, so this comes from a secondary guide.
items.license: Videvo Attribution License / CC BY 3.0 (free); Premium license (paid)

items.name: ActionVFX free collection
items.description: Professional VFX elements (fire, explosions, muzzle flashes and more) in RED/ProRes; free packs and samples need a free account.
items.verdictNote: trial: ActionVFX License Agreement (Individual/Startup/Enterprise; also applies to free downloads)
items.why: Commercial use is allowed in work where you add substantial value, and no attribution is mentioned. Choose the Individual licence for one person (Startup covers companies under $3M). The licence bans standalone redistribution, putting the files into templates or libraries, and using them to train AI or generate media with AI tools.
items.license: ActionVFX License Agreement (Individual/Startup/Enterprise; also applies to free downloads)

items.name: ProductionCrate / FootageCrate (free tier)
items.description: Large VFX, SFX and graphics library; assets without the Pro star icon download free with a Free account.
items.verdictNote: trial: ProductionCrate Free License
items.why: The FAQ states that both the Free and Pro licences allow commercial use in media you create. The homepage doesn't spell out attribution or download limits, so check the full licence before relying on it.

items.name: LottieFiles free animations
items.description: Free public Lottie (JSON) vector animations for web, apps, games and video overlays.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Lottie Simple License
items.why: Commercial use is allowed and attribution is encouraged but optional. If you redistribute the animation files, they must stay under the same licence. You can't scrape the library to build a competing service.

items.name: Kenney Particle Pack
items.description: 80 particle sprites, light cookies and shaders; also available as a ready-made Godot Asset Library package.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0
items.why: Public domain: commercial use is allowed and no attribution is needed.

items.name: Godot Shaders
items.description: Community library of Godot shaders: dissolve, fire, water, outline, post-processing and more.
items.verdictNote: trial: Per shader: CC0, MIT or GPL v3
items.why: Prefer CC0 or MIT shaders for commercial games, since GPL brings copyleft obligations. The licence covers only the shader code: preview images and videos are not included.
items.license: Per shader: CC0, MIT or GPL v3

items.name: Unity VFX Graph samples
items.description: Official Unity Visual Effect Graph sample scenes and effects.
items.verdictNote: reference: Unity Companion License (unconfirmed)
items.why: Probably usable only within Unity: I couldn't open the licence (the mirror redirected), so treat these as learning material, not as assets for Godot.

items.name: Gabriel Aguiar VFX packs
items.description: High-quality stylized Unity VFX packs and tutorials; I found no current free pack (his Asset Store page says 'Live soon'; Gumroad lists the paid Unique Projectiles packs).
items.verdictNote: assess: Unity Asset Store EULA
items.why: Asset Store assets may be used in other engines such as Godot under the EULA, but can't be redistributed as extractable raw files. The packs are paid and built in Unity, so porting them is manual work.

items.name: Sonniss GDC Game Audio Bundle
items.description: A free multi-GB pro SFX bundle released every year (2026: about 7.47 GB from 17 vendors); past years' bundles are archived.
items.verdictNote: adopt: Sonniss GDC bundle royalty-free license
items.why: Commercial use in unlimited projects is allowed with no attribution needed. You can't sell or redistribute the sounds on their own or as a sound library. A 2026 guide reports that Sonniss also bans AI training. Download only from the official site, not from torrents. Licence was read from a third-party copy of the PDF; confirm on the official download page.

items.name: Kenney Audio packs
items.description: About 10 game-ready audio packs: UI, impacts, sci-fi, RPG, casino, jingles and voiceover.
items.verdictNote: adopt: CC0
items.why: Public domain: commercial use is allowed and no attribution is needed. The Kenney logo is reserved for Kenney's own projects.

items.name: BBC Sound Effects
items.description: BBC archive of 33,000+ sound effects.
items.verdictNote: reference: RemArc Licence (personal/educational/research only)
items.why: Free downloads are not cleared for commercial use, so not for monetized YouTube or games. Commercial licences for individual sounds are sold through Pro Sound Effects.

items.name: ZapSplat
items.description: Large SFX and music library; free accounts get MP3s, paid Gold/Premium (around $4-5/mo) adds WAV files and removes the credit requirement.
items.verdictNote: trial: ZapSplat Standard License (free = attribution; Gold = no attribution)
items.why: Commercial use is allowed. The free tier requires a credit to ZapSplat. Embedding in films and games is allowed; standalone redistribution is not, and physical merchandise needs an extra licence.
items.license: ZapSplat Standard License (free = attribution; Gold = no attribution)

items.name: 99Sounds
items.description: Free curated SFX and sample libraries from independent sound designers.
items.verdictNote: adopt: 99Sounds License (royalty-free)
items.why: Commercial use and client work are allowed with no attribution needed. You can't redistribute the files on their own, and the licence bans using them in noise, white-noise or sleep-sound apps.

items.name: Soundly (free tier)
items.description: Desktop sound-library app with a free cloud library and a paid Pro tier; it can also browse Freesound.
items.verdictNote: trial: Soundly EULA
items.why: Soundly's own Free and Pro libraries are cleared for commercial use, including games. Sounds pulled from Freesound keep their own licences; filter to CC0-only to avoid credit requirements.

items.name: Free To Use Sounds
items.description: Field-recording and ambience SFX packs, offered free or pay-what-you-want and also sold on Bandcamp.
items.verdictNote: assess: Royalty-free (exact terms unconfirmed)
items.why: Generally described as royalty-free for commercial use, but I couldn't open their licence page. Confirm the attribution and redistribution terms before relying on it.

items.name: Incompetech (Kevin MacLeod)
items.description: Huge royalty-free music catalogue by Kevin MacLeod, widely used on YouTube and in games.
items.verdictNote: trial: CC BY 4.0 (paid no-attribution license available)
items.why: Commercial use is allowed only with the credit line "Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com)" plus the CC BY 4.0 licence; leaving it out is a copyright violation. A paid Standard licence (about $30+ per track) removes the credit. Very recognisable to viewers.

items.name: YouTube Audio Library
items.description: Free music and SFX inside YouTube Studio, with an 'Attribution not required' filter.
items.verdictNote: adopt: YouTube Audio Library terms (some tracks CC BY)
items.why: Safe for monetized YouTube, and Content ID won't claim these tracks. CC BY tracks need the exact credit in the description. Use outside YouTube, including in games, isn't generally cleared, so don't use these tracks in Godot builds.
items.license: YouTube Audio Library terms (some tracks CC BY)

items.name: Uppbeat
items.description: Creator-focused music and SFX platform; the free plan gives 3 downloads for your own channels, and paid plans start at $6.99/mo.
items.verdictNote: trial: Uppbeat Free / paid licence
items.why: The free plan is limited to individual use on your own channels, and its pricing page doesn't mention Content ID safelisting. Paid plans safelist 1-10 channels. Not intended for distributed games.

items.name: Free Music Archive
items.description: Large archive of independent music under a mix of CC licences.
items.verdictNote: reference: Per track: Creative Commons (BY / BY-SA / BY-NC / BY-ND etc.)
items.why: Many tracks are NC (non-commercial) or ND (no-derivatives) and so are unusable for monetized videos without the artist's written permission. Only BY or BY-SA tracks with credit are safe. FMA can't resolve Content ID claims; you have to contact the artist.
items.license: Per track: Creative Commons (BY / BY-SA / BY-NC / BY-ND etc.)

items.name: Purple Planet Music
items.description: Free production music for video and games from two UK composers.
items.verdictNote: trial: Purple Planet free licence (attribution) / paid licence
items.why: Commercial use is allowed only with a visible credit and link to purple-planet.com. A paid licence (from about $8 per track) removes the credit. No remixing.
items.license: Purple Planet free licence (attribution) / paid licence

items.name: Soundimage.org (Eric Matyas)
items.description: 2,000+ game-oriented music loops and SFX by Eric Matyas.
items.verdictNote: assess: Free with attribution (Soundimage terms)
items.why: Free for games and projects with attribution, and has been used in Steam games. I couldn't open his attribution and licence page, so confirm the commercial terms there.

items.name: GameDevelopmentKit (GDK)
items.description: Unity client plus .NET server framework built on UnityGameFramework and ET 8.1, with HybridCLR hot updates, shared protocols and config, networking, UI and build tooling. Docs in Chinese. About 7,400 files; last commit 2026-10-13.
items.verdictNote: skip: Unity + C# multiplayer framework for experienced teams
items.why: Built for Chinese mobile-MMO-style studios that need hot updates and a game server. Far too heavy for a solo or no-code creator, and it locks you into Unity.

items.name: GDevelop
items.description: [2D, 2.5D, light 3D] Open-source no-code engine: event sheets instead of code, web and desktop editor, exports to web, mobile and desktop. Has an AI chat and an AI agent that builds mechanics, UI and menus from plain-text requests; a real-time 3D editor arrived in 5.6.
items.verdictNote: trial: 2D, 2.5D, light 3D
items.why: The closest thing to a no-code Godot. Study its event-sheet design for how to describe game logic in plain language, which is exactly how you'd prompt Claude. AI credit pricing not confirmed.

items.name: Defold
items.description: [2D (3D capable)] Free engine originally from King (Candy Crush), now run by the Defold Foundation. Lua scripting, tiny builds, strong web and mobile export, message-passing architecture.
items.verdictNote: assess: 2D (3D capable)
items.why: Worth copying for efficiency: very small builds, fast load times and a clean component/message design. Code-first (Lua), so less friendly for a non-coder.

items.name: Phaser
items.description: [2D (web)] The most popular open-source HTML5 2D game framework (JavaScript/TypeScript), with an editor sold separately.
items.verdictNote: assess: 2D (web)
items.why: Huge example library and docs, so Claude writes Phaser well. Best for quick browser games; copy its scene and loader structure for web games.

items.name: LÖVE (Love2D)
items.description: [2D] Minimal Lua 2D framework loved for game jams; Balatro was built with it.
items.verdictNote: reference: 2D
items.why: Proof that a tiny framework is enough for a hit. Read it for the simplest possible game-loop structure.

items.name: Raylib
items.description: [2D and 3D] Small, very readable C library for games, with bindings for 60+ languages and hundreds of examples.
items.verdictNote: reference: 2D and 3D
items.why: The clearest code to learn how an engine works under the hood (window, input, draw loop). Reference, not a production pick for a non-coder.

items.name: MonoGame
items.description: [2D (3D possible)] Open-source C# framework (successor to Microsoft XNA) behind Stardew Valley and Celeste.
items.verdictNote: reference: 2D (3D possible)
items.why: Code-only framework; study how big indie hits structured content pipelines. Too low-level for no-code work.

items.name: Ren'Py
items.description: [2D visual novels] Python-based visual novel engine used by thousands of commercial games.
items.verdictNote: assess: 2D visual novels
items.why: Ideal if a project is story-first (comics, interactive stories). Its simple script format is a good model for AI-written dialogue.

items.name: Bevy
items.description: [2D and 3D] Data-driven Rust engine built around an Entity Component System (ECS); no editor yet.
items.verdictNote: reference: 2D and 3D
items.why: Best place to learn ECS architecture and data-oriented efficiency. Rust and no editor make it impractical for a non-coder.

items.name: Unity
items.description: [2D, 2.5D, 3D] The most widely used commercial engine, especially for mobile and 2.5D; huge asset store and tutorials.
items.verdictNote: reference: 2D, 2.5D, 3D
items.why: Largest tutorial and asset ecosystem to learn techniques from. Closed source and past pricing controversy; check Unity's pricing page for the current Personal revenue cap before committing.
items.license: Proprietary; Personal plan free under a revenue cap, no runtime fee (cancelled Sept 2024)

items.name: Unreal Engine
items.description: [3D (2.5D via Paper2D/HD-2D)] Epic's AAA engine: Nanite, Lumen, MetaHuman, Blueprints visual scripting. Source viewable on GitHub after linking an Epic account.
items.verdictNote: reference: 3D (2.5D via Paper2D/HD-2D)
items.why: Best to copy high-end techniques (lighting, cinematic cameras, Blueprints patterns). Heavy for an 8 GB laptop GPU; its source can't be copied into other engines.
items.license: Proprietary, source available; 5% royalty above $1M gross per product

items.name: GameMaker
items.description: [2D] Long-running 2D engine with its own GML language and drag-and-drop; Undertale and Hotline Miami used it.
items.verdictNote: reference: 2D
items.why: Free tier can't be used for commercial games. Good 2D workflow ideas, but Godot is free for commercial use.
items.license: Proprietary; free = non-commercial only, Professional one-time purchase for commercial

items.name: Construct 3
items.description: [2D] Browser-based no-code 2D engine using event sheets.
items.verdictNote: assess: 2D
items.why: Polished no-code option, but a paid subscription; GDevelop gives a similar approach for free.

items.name: Flax Engine
items.description: [3D] C#/C++ 3D engine with a Unity-like editor and full source on GitHub.
items.verdictNote: reference: 3D
items.why: Readable modern 3D engine source with a lower royalty than Unreal. Small community.
items.license: Source available; free for non-commercial; 4% royalty on earnings above $250k per quarter

items.name: Open 3D Engine (O3DE)
items.description: [3D] Linux Foundation open-source AAA engine, successor to Amazon Lumberyard.
items.verdictNote: skip: 3D
items.why: Powerful but heavy and complex, aimed at studios; not for a solo creator.

items.name: Stride
items.description: [2D and 3D] Open-source C# engine (formerly Xenko) with a full editor.
items.verdictNote: reference: 2D and 3D
items.why: Clean C# engine to study; small community compared with Godot.

items.name: PlayCanvas
items.description: [3D (web)] WebGL/WebGPU engine with a collaborative browser editor; used for web games and product configurators.
items.verdictNote: assess: 3D (web)
items.why: Good model for fast-loading 3D on the web; the cloud editor's free tier makes projects public.

items.name: Wicked Engine
items.description: [3D] One-person open-source C++ engine with a modern renderer (ray tracing, GPU-driven rendering).
items.verdictNote: reference: 3D
items.why: Shows how much efficiency a small, focused codebase can reach; reference for rendering techniques only.

items.name: Excalibur.js
items.description: [2D (web)] TypeScript-first 2D web game engine with good docs.
items.verdictNote: reference: 2D (web)
items.why: Clean TypeScript structure to copy for web games; smaller than Phaser.

items.name: KAPLAY
items.description: [2D (web)] Beginner-friendly JavaScript game library (community fork of Kaboom.js) with very short, readable code.
items.verdictNote: assess: 2D (web)
items.why: Very short code makes it ideal for AI-generated prototypes and teaching.

items.name: Wan2.2 LightX2V distill (4-step LoRAs)
items.why: 4-step distill for Wan 2.2 A14B; ~10x fewer steps than 40-step runs, which makes A14B usable on GPU-poor boxes via GGUF + RAM offload.

items.name: LTX-2.5 GGUF quants (community)
items.why: Smallest distilled files ~11.5-12.6 GB plus a large Gemma text encoder; not an 8 GB option, plan for 16-24 GB GPUs.

items.name: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 (Meituan)
items.description: Open audio-driven avatar video model built on LongCat-Video: photo + audio (or text + audio) to a talking or singing person, 480p or 720p, English and Chinese, two-person scenes, long clips via segment continuation. 8-step distilled mode and INT8 option; ComfyUI node by smthemex. Hosted on WaveSpeedAI at $0.04/s (480p) or $0.08/s (720p), 3 s minimum.
items.verdictNote: trial: test on WaveSpeed first; self-host on a rented 48 GB GPU only if volume justifies it
items.why: MIT weights and strong identity hold from a single photo (a hands-on review kept one face across 82 s). But it needed about 40 GB VRAM even with INT8 and distillation, and took roughly 44 s of GPU time per 1 s of video, so it cannot run on an 8 GB or likely a 24 GB card. It does not clone voices: supply your own audio.
items.cost: free (self-host GPU) / about $0.04-0.08 per second hosted

items.name: NVIDIA MotionBricks
items.description: Real-time generative motion model (about 224M params) from NVIDIA research (SIGGRAPH 2026): given recent poses and target poses it generates the in-between movement, with 'smart primitives' for navigation and object interaction. Weights for SOMA human skeleton and Unitree G1 robot; ONNX and TensorRT runtime. NVIDIA reports 15,000 FPS and 2 ms latency on an RTX 5090. Code lives in NVlabs/GR00T-WholeBodyControl.
items.verdictNote: assess: research preview; watch for a Godot/Unity/Unreal bridge
items.why: Could replace hand-built animation state machines, and the weights allow commercial use. Today it is a Linux, NVIDIA-only Python preview with no game-engine plugin, outputs poses for its own skeletons (retargeting to other rigs is unsolved), and the bundled sample motions are evaluation-only. Mixamo or Mesh2Motion clips remain the practical route for now.
items.license: Code Apache-2.0; weights NVIDIA Open Model Agreement (commercial use allowed); sample motions evaluation-only

items.name: CosyVoice2 / CosyVoice 3
items.why: Free local zero-shot voice clone on 8 GB; real use shows dropped/garbled brand names and short questions, so it needs a seeds + whisper-gate + splice workflow.
items.source: research 2026-10-27: voice tiers + mascot lip-sync for WFF shorts

items.name: IndexTTS2
items.why: Emotion-controllable zero-shot TTS with low WER in one 2026 eval; VRAM (6-14 GB) and license are unverified.
items.source: research 2026-10-27: voice tiers + mascot lip-sync for WFF shorts

items.name: Seed-VC
items.why: Zero-shot voice conversion that could be layered over a TTS take for timbre; no evidence yet that it adds naturalness.
items.source: research 2026-10-27: voice tiers + mascot lip-sync for WFF shorts

items.name: anymove (creature mocap from AI video)
items.description: Generates motion for any rigged creature from one AI video showing two camera views in a single frame: a DINOv2-based joint reader finds joints in both views and fits the rig frame by frame, output an animated 24 fps GLB. Uses Tripo H3.1 (mesh), FLUX 3, MiniMax H3 video on fal (about $0.26 per 5 s clip), Blender 5. Training the reader needs a 24 GB GPU; fitting runs on less. 4 commits.
items.verdictNote: reference: clever pipeline idea, too early to use
items.why: Covers non-human creatures, which Mixamo and Mesh2Motion don't, but it is a 1-star, 4-commit experiment that depends on paid fal APIs. Revisit once it matures; Mesh2Motion stays the practical route.
items.license: Apache-2.0 (code); MiniMax H3 community licence for the bundled LoRA

items.name: GroundAnything (GroundingPI)
items.description: ~4-5B visual grounding model (Qwen3-4B backbone + Kimi-K3 vision encoder): finds objects, referring expressions, points, OCR text, document layout and GUI elements from natural language; a parallel (diffusion-style) decoder and an autoregressive VLM variant. Paper 2026-09-30, weights 2026-10-14. Publisher reports 72.4% across 30 grounding benchmarks (VLM variant). Tested on datacenter GPUs; no VRAM figure given.
items.verdictNote: assess: strong open grounding model, but check the Kimi licence and VRAM first
items.why: Useful for agents that must click GUI elements or crop products from images. Brand new, benchmarks are self-reported, and the Kimi licence terms carry through, so read them before commercial use.
items.license: Apache-2.0 for original parts; Kimi K3 License applies to the combined model

items.name: solidcv (solidSF)
items.description: Pure-Rust computer-vision library pitched as an OpenCV replacement (features, stereo, pose, optical flow, 3D octrees). Targets Apple Silicon and NVIDIA Grace-Blackwell. 8 commits; benchmarks compare against hard-coded OpenCV numbers. Sister repos claim video-to-CAD/CAE but have 2 stars each.
items.verdictNote: skip: early, and the fast engines are a paid cloud API
items.why: Too early and partly metered through paid 'solidSF Credits'. For video or photo to CAD, text-to-cad is the more mature option already in the library.

items.name: OpenPencil (ZSeven-W)
items.description: Open-source AI-native vector design tool: describe a UI and it appears as editable layers on a canvas; select an element and ask chat to change it; edit by hand; export code (React + Tailwind, HTML + CSS, Vue, Svelte, Flutter, SwiftUI, Compose, React Native) or images/PDF. Built-in MCP server installs into Claude Code, Codex and others; desktop apps for macOS, Windows, Linux, plus web app and CLI. Bring your own AI provider key.
items.verdictNote: trial: free editable canvas for landing pages and tool sites, driven from Claude Code
items.why: This is the tool in the post. Unlike prompt-only builders you get real editable layers before exporting code, and it is free. Pair it with the MotionSites skill's spec-and-screenshot loop for quality; check exported code before shipping.

items.name: open-pencil (Figma-compatible editor)
items.description: Open-source design editor that reads and writes native Figma .fig files (and .pen), with an AI chat assistant (100+ tools, your own OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenRouter key), an MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor and Windsurf, HTML/Tailwind export and HTML-to-layers import. Desktop (Tauri) and web/PWA.
items.verdictNote: assess: pick this one if you need to open or hand off Figma files
items.why: Same-sounding name as OpenPencil but a different project; its strength is Figma file compatibility. Choose one of the two, not both.

items.name: vibe-knowledge (sourced explainer videos)
items.description: Claude Code skill that turns one knowledge topic into a narrated short video where every sentence carries a source: topic choice, fact-check, script, voiceover, code-rendered frames at 1080p60 in 44 visual styles, QA and a publishing pack, with confirmation checkpoints. Optional paid tier generates AI shots through the Renoise MCP with a cost estimate first. Chinese README with an English version. 3 commits.
items.verdictNote: assess: good pattern for fact-checked education Shorts; very new
items.why: The sourced-sentence and checkpoint design fits finance and science education content where accuracy matters. Only 3 commits and 14 stars, so test it on one topic and read the scripts before relying on it.

items.name: DSH Blender plugin
items.description: Lets an AI drive Blender 4.x/5.x over a direct TCP channel (16 tools: viewport capture, scene edits, render profiling, decimation, headless renders) instead of MCP; requires DSH (DeepSeek Harness) and Node 20+. Free, donation-funded.
items.verdictNote: skip: tied to DeepSeek Harness; blender-mcp already covers Claude
items.why: Built for a different agent harness. blender-mcp (adopt) does the same job inside Claude.

items.name: Rikyu
items.description: AI design service for businesses without a designer: logos, ads, print, websites, apps, 3D and video from a description, also usable over MCP from Claude, Codex and Cursor. Free tier is personal use only; commercial use starts with paid plans (the $5 Basic plan is no longer offered).
items.verdictNote: reference: Claude's own design tools, Canva and OpenPencil cover this for free
items.why: Convenient all-in-one, but the free tier can't be used commercially and the maker is a single developer with no company named. Nothing it does is missing from the current stack.
items.cost: Free 3,000 credits (personal use only); Pro $20/mo; Max $50/mo

items.name: AI Pose Gallery (Chinese mirror)
items.description: Static gallery of AI pose reference images (README: 288 pose groups, 1,439 images) translated into Chinese from a Japanese original. The images belong to the original author and are not licensed for reuse; some categories are adult-oriented.
items.verdictNote: skip: no image licence; use your own references
items.why: Fine to browse for inspiration, but you can't reuse the images, and the adult categories make it unsuitable for brand work.

items.name: Polyfork
items.description: 2,700+ free low-poly 3D assets and themed kits (+1,468 HD editions on Pro), each built as a small program with typed 'knobs' (colours, proportions, part counts, state, wear) published as JSON so AI tools can set them. Downloads include GLB, FBX, USDZ, OBJ and a three.js ES module with a ready index.html; works in three.js, Godot, Unity, Unreal, Blender, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas. Won the Build with Gemini XPRIZE; built by Lucas Martinic. Sign-in with Google or email link.
items.verdictNote: adopt: free, commercial, and parametric, so Claude can generate variants for web and Godot games
items.why: Like Kenney, but every asset can be re-coloured and re-shaped by an agent through its knobs, which suits three.js mini-games and quick Godot prototypes. Catches: custom licence (not CC0), so don't commit the raw files to a public repo, and HD editions are paid.
items.license: Polyfork licence: commercial use, no attribution; no resale or redistribution of the assets; no use to build or train a commercial 3D-asset generator
items.cost: Free low-poly tier; Pro $15/mo (HD editions); Lifetime $100 (limited seats)

items.name: tongjiang-lab (3D science lessons)
items.description: 55 free interactive 3D high-school science lessons (physics, chemistry, biology, geography), each a single offline HTML file built with three.js; Chinese interface, aligned to Chinese PEP 2019 textbooks. 3 commits.
items.verdictNote: reference: a good pattern for single-file interactive explainers; non-commercial content
items.why: Shows how far one self-contained HTML file can go for interactive teaching, a format worth copying for education content. The lessons themselves are non-commercial and in Chinese, so use them for ideas, not reuse.

items.name: Ultra-Water (three.js ocean)
items.description: Real-time ocean renderer for three.js (WebGL2) with a demo island: FFT waves, shore breakers, foam, caustics, underwater view, buoyant floating objects, procedural island and sky. npm install / npm run dev. Benchmarked only on Chrome with an RTX 3060. 9 commits; largely AI-assisted per its README. Missing: boat wakes, object-to-object collisions, curling breaking waves.
items.verdictNote: assess: copy its water techniques into a three.js scene; not a maintained library
items.why: Tried 2026-10-28: the full renderer (~190k-vertex grid, FFT cascades) is too heavy for a phone game, but its techniques port well at small scale. A lite re-write (polar grid, GPU Gerstner waves damped near the coast, analytic noise normals, Fresnel sky reflection, glints, coast-distance foam bands, two-phase river flow, CPU twin for floating props) held 60 fps on desktop and Pixel 7 emulation in a three.js r160 farm game. Copy techniques, not the code.

items.name: mogfield (ComfyUI video studio UI)
items.description: Open-source web studio (Vite + React, Hono server, Node 22+) that wraps ComfyUI workflows in a simple UI: text/frame/reference video generation with Extend, Re-shoot and Restyle; images and character reference sheets; Character Swap into phone footage; a media library that pulls TikTok/Instagram/X links with yt-dlp; a beta storyboard agent. Runs on Comfy Cloud (partner models such as Seedance, FLUX 3 and MiniMax billed to your Comfy account) or on your own ComfyUI; an ffmpeg preview mode works without a GPU. Source checked: no install hooks, ffmpeg called with argument lists; Instagram links can require browser cookies.
items.verdictNote: reference: borrow its UI flows for Content Studio AI; don't run it as-is
items.why: Nice ideas for a creator-facing front end over ComfyUI (extend, re-shoot, restyle, character sheets), which Content Studio AI could copy. But it is a 1-star, days-old project; Character Swap into real footage needs the filmed person's consent; and re-using downloaded TikTok/Instagram clips raises copyright and platform-terms issues. Never hand it your main browser's cookies.
items.license: MIT (bundled node pack has its own licence; model weights each their own)
